teaching.hint: For a starred element, separate the cases of using zero copies and consuming one more matching character.

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A star creates overlapping repeat-or-skip choices, so prefix dynamic programming captures all possibilities without exponential recomputation.
solution_outline.approach: Let dp[i][j] state whether the first i input characters match the first j pattern characters. A literal or dot uses the diagonal predecessor when the current characters match. For x*, combine the zero-copy state that removes x* with the state that consumes one matching input character while retaining x*. Initialize the empty-input row for chains of starred elements.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each DP entry is true exactly when its two prefixes fully match; transitions use only smaller input prefixes, smaller pattern prefixes, or both.
solution_outline.correctness: A non-star pattern suffix has only the case of matching its final token and reducing both prefixes. Any match ending in x* uses either zero x values or at least one; those exhaustive cases are represented by removing x* or consuming one input character while keeping it. Induction over prefix lengths therefore makes every DP state, including the final one, exact.
solution_outline.complexity: O(|s||p|) time and O(|p|) auxiliary space with row compression; O(|s||p|) space is also valid.
solution_outline.pitfall: Failing to initialize patterns such as a*b* against an empty input loses valid zero-repetition matches.

accepted_alternatives: Top-down recursion with memoization over input and pattern indices using the same repeat-or-skip cases.
common_wrong_turns: Greedily consuming as many starred characters as possible
Treating star as an independent token
Performing substring matching instead of full matching
source_fidelity_notes: Examples were omitted; full-match semantics, both operator definitions, pattern validity, character domains, and length bounds were retained.
